summary:
MARSAD is an interactive astronomical research platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the “Planet X and SPHEREx” challenge.

The main goal of MARSAD is to make complex astronomical data easier to explore, understand, and analyze through a single interactive web application.

Our project focuses on SPHEREx, a NASA space telescope that observes the entire sky using infrared light and analyzes it across 102 different spectral bands. This allows scientists to study celestial objects and discover important changes in the universe.

MARSAD focuses on five astronomical targets: Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi B, WISE 0855, RW Aurigae, and R Draconis.

The platform provides several powerful tools, including an interactive Sky Map, Timeline for comparing observations over time, Motion Vectors for tracking object movement, Light Curve analysis for studying brightness variations, and 102-Band Spectra for exploring the properties of celestial objects.

It also includes asteroid tracking and Data Lineage to help users understand where the information comes from and how it is processed.

Ultimately, MARSAD aims to connect scientific data with an accessible and interactive experience, making space exploration easier for everyone.
details:
MARSAD – Project Description

MARSAD is an interactive astronomical research platform designed to help users explore, analyze, and understand complex astronomical data, particularly data from NASA's SPHEREx space telescope.

The platform works by collecting and processing astronomical datasets and presenting them through an interactive web interface. It focuses on five astronomical targets and provides several scientific analysis tools, including an interactive Sky Map, Timeline Comparison, Motion Vectors, Light Curves, 102-Band Spectral Analysis, and Solar System object tracking. These features allow users to investigate celestial objects, compare observations across different periods, study their movements, analyze brightness variations, and explore their spectral characteristics.

The main benefit of MARSAD is making advanced astronomical information more accessible, organized, and understandable. Instead of requiring users to work directly with complicated scientific datasets, MARSAD transforms the information into interactive visualizations that support exploration and scientific investigation.

Our intended impact is to encourage interest in astronomy, support educational activities, and provide a user-friendly environment for exploring real astronomical observations. We aim to bridge the gap between complex scientific data and the general public.

The project was developed using modern web technologies, including React, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, alongside data-processing tools and scientific visualization libraries. We also considered astronomical datasets, APIs, and scientific data formats such as FITS when designing the platform.

What makes MARSAD creative is the integration of multiple astronomical analysis tools into one unified experience. Rather than presenting isolated charts and images, it connects different types of observations to help users build a broader understanding of each astronomical target.

During development, our team considered scientific accuracy, data reliability, usability, accessibility, performance, visual clarity, and the ability to expand the platform with additional astronomical datasets and analysis features.
